claims.text: The reported initial TiVNbTa alloy has a single-phase, dendritic BCC microstructure.
The reported TiVNbTa alloy has a yield strength of approximately 330 MPa at 1273 K.
The reported TiVNbTa alloy has a compressive strength of approximately 423 MPa at 1273 K.
The reported TiVNbTa alloy sustains about 30% strain at 1273 K.
Adding less than 1 wt% Y2O3 nano-oxides to TiVNbTa will mitigate high-temperature softening.
Y2O3 nano-oxides can be introduced during vacuum arc melting under regulated oxygen partial pressure.
A homogenization anneal at approximately 1273 K, together with advanced processing controls, will produce uniform oxide dispersion and suitable interfacial bonding.
The intervention will create uniformly distributed nanoscale Y2O3 particles embedded in the BCC TiVNbTa matrix.
The dispersed Y2O3 particles will provide pinning sites for dislocations.
The dispersed Y2O3 particles will stabilize grain boundaries.
The nano-oxides will impede dislocation motion through Orowan strengthening.
The nano-oxides will inhibit grain-boundary migration and reduce thermally driven microstructural coarsening.
Reduced dislocation motion and microstructural coarsening will preserve the alloy's high-temperature yield and compressive strengths.
The Y2O3-modified alloy is expected to exceed 500 MPa yield strength at 1273 K, compared with the stated 330 MPa baseline.
The intervention is expected to improve compressive strength at 1273 K.
The intervention is expected to cause only minimal loss of ductility under cyclic thermal-mechanical loading.
The magnitude of strengthening depends on the quality of Y2O3 dispersion and particle-matrix interfacial bonding.
Long-term stability of the modified alloy under cyclic thermal conditions has not been confirmed.
